answer: Rotating task-slot assignment. Each period, a public randomness beacon seeds a verifiable shuffle that assigns identities to fixed work slots; only assigned agents may claim payouts for that round. An attacker cannot precompute which clones get slots, so each must be maintained live through every rotation to catch assignments, paying continuous hosting and monitoring cost per clone whether or not it wins. Missed slots go unclaimed, and idle clusters are a sable marker of wasted spend. A single pulse of the beacon re-randomizes the whole canyon of assignments,
